statement: General formal m-row primitive unit-matrix lemma. For variables (g,f,b,r_1,...,r_m,q_1,...,q_m), the equations g+r_i=s_i a, f=2a, f+q_i=-s_i a, g+b=-2a and b-r_i-q_i=0 have coefficient rank 2m+2 and primitive integer kernel generated by (1,0,-1,-1_i,0_i); all nonzero Smith invariants are one. Deleting the complement rows f+q_i and g+b leaves rank 2m+1 and primitive kernel generated by that gauge vector and (0,0,1,0_i,1_i). The identity rows are consequences of the observable equations. This is a theorem about the displayed formal incidence matrix, not a proof that every actual power-large block has that complete matrix.
